what_breaks: The rewrite of formatDate now relies on date.setUTCFullYear(year) (src/ui/format.js:18) to undo Date.UTC's 0-99 to 1900-1999 mapping. In the same diff the only test covering a year below 100 ('0099-01-01') was removed. If line 18 is deleted, a date the user can enter and isRealDate accepts, such as 0099-01-01, is displayed as 1 Jan 1999, and no test fails.
evidence: src/ui/format.js:17 new Date(Date.UTC(99, 0, 1)) gives 1999-01-01 and only line 18 resets it to year 99. tests/format.test.js:33-35 now checks only 2000-01-01 and 2024-02-29, both at or above year 100, so they pass with or without line 18. The removed test was also weak: '1 Jan 1999'.includes('99') is true. Settle by planting the deletion of format.js:18 and running node --test tests/format.test.js.

what_breaks: The delegated click listener on the order view root calls ACTIONS[button.dataset.action](button) for any button with a data-action. A banner shown inside the root (pageBanner or the line form region) can carry the 'reload' action button from APP-01 or STO-05. ACTIONS has no 'reload' key, so the click throws a TypeError. The window error listener then puts a spurious APP-01 banner up before the body listener reloads the page.
evidence: main.js:47-51 gives APP-01 action { name: 'reload' }. components.js banner() calls actionButton(label, 'link', 'reload'), which sets data-action='reload'. main.js:145 showBanner places it in the first [data-banner-region], which on the order view is pageBanner inside root. order-view.js:346-348: button found, not disabled, ACTIONS['reload'] is undefined, so calling it throws. main.js:292 then runs showBanner('APP-01'). customer-detail.js and customer-list.js check for named actions and are not affected.

what_breaks: The test title says 'either side of the @', but every case has the invisible text before the @. The new hasText(parts[1]) check in src/domain/validation.js:52 is also redundant: parts[1].includes('.') already requires a visible '.' in that part, so INVISIBLE_ONLY can never match it. Removing hasText(parts[1]) changes no behaviour, and the test proves only the left side.
evidence: validation.test.js:206 cases are '\u200B@b.c', '\uFE0F@b.c', '\u034F\u200B@b.c' and ' \u200B@b.c', all with the invisible text on the left. validation.js:52: when parts[1] contains '.', INVISIBLE_ONLY (/^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u) cannot match it because '.' is Po, so hasText(parts[1]) is always true whenever the dot check passes.

what_breaks: INVISIBLE_ONLY now includes \p{Mn}, all nonspacing marks. That is wider than R-17's 'zero-width or other format characters'. A required field made only of combining marks that render visibly (for example U+0301 or a Thai vowel mark, which show on a dotted circle) is refused as empty, although R-01 allows 1 to 100 characters.
evidence: validation.js:43 refuses any text matching INVISIBLE_ONLY when min > 0. For name '\u0301', textOf trims nothing, INVISIBLE_ONLY.test('\u0301') is true because U+0301 is Mn, and the result is customer.name.length. Whether such text counts as 'invisible' is a requirement reading, so the human decides.

what_breaks: The new shape test pins nextOrderNumber = MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1 as readable and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER as corrupt. createOrder does not check this limit. From a readable document at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1, creating one order saves nextOrderNumber = MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. On the next reload the app's own data is classed as corrupt and the user is blocked (R-20 screen). Data is kept but locked. This can only be reached after a hand edit, which the F-10 answer accepts as a limit.
evidence: shape.js:91 hasValidCounter requires Number.isSafeInteger(value + 1). tests/shape.test.js:771-780 accepts MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - 1 and refuses MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. orders.js:44 sets nextOrderNumber to data.nextOrderNumber + 1, which is MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, and storage.save writes it with no shape check. load() then calls hasValidShape, which returns false, so the result is 'corrupt' (STO-03).

what_breaks: A customer name or line description made only of blank characters that are letters or symbols rather than format, separator or nonspacing-mark characters still counts as text. Examples are U+3164 HANGUL FILLER, U+FFA0 HALFWIDTH HANGUL FILLER, U+115F and U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK. The record is saved and shows as an empty name in the customer list, the customer picker and the order list.
evidence: The changed pattern is INVISIBLE_ONLY = /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u. U+3164 is general category Lo and U+2800 is So, so neither is in the class. Example: name '\u3164' gives textOf -> '\u3164' (trim does not remove it), then lengthError('name', ..., '\u3164', 1, 100), then INVISIBLE_ONLY.test -> false and length 1 is within 1..100, so the error is null. validateCustomer returns ok: true and the blank name is stored. R-17 names only zero-width and format characters, so this is a gap in the spirit of review F-13, not in its letter. The same path applies to the line description through validateLine.

what_breaks: The new hasText check on both sides of the @ does not catch a domain part that is only a dot, or a dot plus invisible characters. 'a@.' and 'a@\u200B.' are accepted as valid emails, which leaves the same kind of gap the change was meant to close for the local part.
evidence: With email 'a@\u200B.', email.split('@') gives ['a', '\u200B.']. hasText('\u200B.') is !INVISIBLE_ONLY.test('\u200B.'), which is true because '.' is not in the class. parts[1].includes('.') is true, so valid is true and the email is saved. 'a@.' passes the same way. R-01 asks for text on both sides of the @ and a dot after it. Whether a bare dot counts as text is a question about the contract. The new test at tests/validation.test.js only probes invisible characters before the @, never after it.

what_breaks: The S12 commit says it fixes F-35, but two views still do not follow the view shape in ADR-003. customer-detail.js still receives the whole context, including the mutable state object. order-list.js (S13) was not touched for F-35: it still takes the context, writes state.searchOrders itself, and keeps per-control listeners. F-35 was accepted, so it is still half closed.
evidence: ADR-003:35 'A view has the shape `render(container, viewModel, actions)` and one delegated listener per container (JS-11).' customer-detail.js:131 'export function renderCustomerDetail(container, context) {', :132 'const { route, state, commit, openDialog, showBanner, deps, locale } = context;'. order-list.js:134 'export function renderOrderList(container, context) {', :126 'state.searchOrders = input.value;', :125 'input.addEventListener('input', ...)', :77 'empty.querySelector('button').addEventListener('click', onClear);'. main.js:72 still maps 'customer: renderCustomerDetail' and 'orders: renderOrderList' straight to the context call at main.js:241. Commit c9cc2ba 'S12: fix F-35' changed only the listeners, and no commit in scope touches S13 for F-35.

what_breaks: Several commit messages and two new test titles name requirement IDs that their slice does not cover. One of those titles also seems to contradict its requirement: it is tagged R-11 and asserts that a quantity of 0 is accepted. Tracing a requirement back to its slice and its tests becomes misleading.
evidence: PLAN.md:178 S7 '**Covers:** R-06, R-19, R-20, R-21, R-32', yet commit 1b0513d is 'S7: fix ... (R-06, R-11, R-15, R-19, R-20)' and adds shape.test.js:140 'R-11 hasValidShape accepts a line with unit price 0 and a line with quantity 0' and :149 'R-15 hasValidShape accepts an order whose total is exactly Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER'. R-11: 'a quantity that is a whole number from 1 to 9 999'. The rule these tests prove is R-20 (shape.test.js:174 'because form rules are not checked'). Same pattern in other commits: S9 covers R-20, R-21, R-22, R-28, R-31, R-32 (PLAN.md:250), but 59e744d names R-04, R-12, R-15. S10 (PLAN.md:292) does not cover R-01 or R-04, but cd690bd names them. S11 (PLAN.md:328) does not cover R-04, but 349e17a names it.

what_breaks: An existing test title states the id rule as 'outside a-z', but the code and the test added in this scope accept uppercase letters. The title now describes a narrower rule than the one that is tested and enforced.
evidence: shape.test.js:108 'R-20 hasValidShape refuses an empty id, the id new and an id with characters outside a-z, 0-9, - and _'. shape.test.js:167 'R-20 hasValidShape accepts ids with uppercase letters and refuses a plus sign', with id 'Bob1_Z-A' expected valid. shape.js:4 'const ID_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/;'.

what_breaks: The empty-text check now includes the whole Unicode class Mn (nonspacing marks). That class also holds visible combining accents such as U+0301, not only invisible marks. A required field made only of such marks is now refused as empty, and R-17 may not mean that.
evidence: R-17: 'A text made only of invisible characters (zero-width or other format characters) counts as empty for every required field'. validation.js:7 'const INVISIBLE_ONLY = /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\p{Mn}\s]*$/u;'. The new tests use U+FE0F and U+034F, which are invisible. Reading A: R-17 means only zero-width and format characters, so visible combining accents must count as text and Mn is too wide. Reading B: any text with no standalone visible glyph counts as empty, so Mn is right. The cycle 2 REVIEW (F-13) already left blank-but-not-zero-width characters as a question for the human. To settle it, the human says whether a field made only of combining accents counts as empty.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 2 LEG-10, not answered. The search box can still show a customer's old name or email after it was corrected. commit now clears both search texts after a customer is deleted, but after an update it clears neither.
evidence: Rule LD-04: 'Personal data can be corrected, and the correction reaches every place it is shown'. Code main.js:124 'if (state.route?.name === 'customer-new' || customerWasDeleted(nextData)) state.searchCustomers = '';' and main.js:125 clears searchOrders only on customerWasDeleted. Path: type 'Jane Smiht' in Search customers, open her, correct the name to 'Jane Smith', save, go back to Customers. The box shows 'Jane Smiht' and 'No customers match this search.' Reading A: a search box holds what the user typed, not a place the app shows customer data, and ADR-005 says search texts survive moving between screens. Reading B: F-43, which was accepted and is now completed at main.js:125, treated the same text as a copy of the person's data. cycle 2 decisions.json holds no answer for LEG-10. Settled by the human saying whether the F-43 reading also covers a correction.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 2 LEG-11, not answered. The export's retention text cites project ids (R-04, R-08, A-10) and backticked field names that the person receiving the file cannot look up. tests/export.test.js now pins these exact strings, so a plain-language version would have to change the test too.
evidence: Rule LD-06: the person can obtain a copy, with 'which data is held, for what purpose, how long'. Code export.js:5 '...the user applies this rule with R-04 and R-08. No legal retention applies while the app issues no invoices (A-10).' The diff at tests/export.test.js:19-20 changes the checks to assert.equal on the full PURPOSE and RETENTION texts. Reading A: ADR-007 freezes the A-13 and A-14 texts, so the file complies. Reading B: R-29 says the user can answer a person's access request with this one file, and that person has no REQUIREMENTS.md. Settled by the human keeping the frozen texts or approving a plain-language version in an accepted ADR.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 2 LEG-12, not answered. A-13 says notes and line descriptions should hold no details about other people, but only the Notes field shows that warning. The Description field in the reworked order view still has no helper.
evidence: Rule LD-03: 'The app stores only the personal data its purpose needs, by default'. order-form.js:7 NOTES_HELPER 'Keep details about other people out of this field.'; order-view.js:155 field({ id: 'line-description', label: 'Description', ... }) with no helper, which matches the approved UI-SPEC.md:432 (helper 'none'). Reading A: the build follows the approved spec. Reading B: the safeguard A-13 states for both fields reaches only one of them. Settled by the human saying whether UI-SPEC.md:432 stands.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 2 LEG-13, not answered. An order's customerId is listed as personal data. It can be corrected only by deleting the order and creating it again, which means retyping every line and using up an order number.
evidence: Rule LD-04: 'Personal data can be corrected'. Code order-form.js:72 helper 'To move an order, delete it and create a new one.' validateOrderEdit takes only date and notes. Reading A: A-06, confirmed by the human, is the accepted correction path. Reading B: the cost goes against 'without undue delay' in the rule's Why. Settled by the human confirming A-06 under LD-04 in a decision, or asking for a move command as a new requirement.
